correctness.rationale: Under the stated invariance and nonzero generator-image hypotheses the integrable, zero-mean L psi has a positive level set {L psi >= epsilon} of measure p>0 for some epsilon>0. The all-in-set IID event has probability p^m and the fitted generator on it is at least a epsilon/(b^2+gamma)>0 for any finite nonnegative ridge. Reusing the fitted Richardson step makes the prediction grow geometrically on that event; L^2 contractivity and the reverse triangle inequality give the same type of lower bound for the true forecast error. In the circle case the pointwise ratio is at least 1/3 on a set of mass 1/3, and Gram weights average this ratio when the ridge is zero. Direct integration gives G=9/2 and H=-1/2, so the population step 1-h/9+h^2/162 contracts for exactly 0<h<18. These calculations give the stated circle lower bound for all h>0 and k>=0, not an exact risk or a statement about almost every fit. General fixed-k risks need not be finite under the stated hypotheses; they are finite in the smooth circle example.
